latest_release.name: v12.7.0
latest_release.body:
### ⚠️ Potential Breaking Changes

**Improved typing of `@directus/env` to contain known env vars and added `milliseconds` and `bytes` cast types for human... ([#28282](https://github.com/directus/directus/pull/28282))**
Env vars are now cast more strictly:

- Booleans only accept `true`, `false`, `1` and `0` (case-insensitive). Other values (eg `yes`) are invalid, where some
  vars previously treated any non-empty value as enabled (eg `SERVE_APP=FALSE`)
- Plain number durations (eg `ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL=900`) are read as milliseconds, use a unit to be explicit (eg `15m`)
- Invalid values log a warning and fall back to the default (or `false` for booleans without one)
- Variables without a value in a `.env` file (eg `KEY=`) are treated as not configured and fall back to the default. Use
  `KEY=""` for an empty value, eg `DB_PASSWORD=""` for a database user without a password, as `DB_PASSWORD=` is now
  reported as missing
- Empty values of string and list vars (eg `KEY=""` in a `.env` file or `KEY=` in the process environment) are kept as an
  empty string or list instead of falling back to the default, eg an empty `EMAIL_SENDMAIL_PATH` is no longer replaced by
  `/usr/sbin/sendmail`. Empty values of other vars still fall back to the default
- `useEnv` returns parsed values: durations and sizes are numbers, lists are arrays
- The `env` passed to API extensions is typed as `Record<string, unknown>` instead of `Record<string, any>`, so env vars
  need to be narrowed before use

**Bounded the work that parsing query parameters can cause ([#28521](https://github.com/directus/directus/pull/28521))**
`filter` and `deep` are now rejected with an `InvalidQueryError` once they exceed a limit on total node count or nesting depth.

The node allowance is spent across a whole query, so a filter nested under `deep` draws from what is left rather than starting over. Set a limit to `Infinity` to opt out of it.

- `QUERY_FILTER_MAX_NODES` (default `10000`) — total `filter`/`deep` nodes
- `QUERY_FILTER_MAX_DEPTH` (default `50`) — nesting depth of a filter or of `deep`
- `GRAPHQL_QUERY_SELECTION_LIMIT` (default `10000`) — fields a GraphQL operation may select across all its root fields once its fragments are expanded, checked during validation

`QUERY_FILTER_MAX_NODES` is the one most likely to be reached. Every object, array and value counts,
so `{"id":{"_in":[…]}}` costs one node per value plus three, and an `_in` of more than 9997 values is
rejected.

A `$NOW(...)` adjustment longer than 64 characters is now treated as unparseable, which also rejects
a zero-padded amount that long, such as `$NOW(0000…0005s)`. A dynamic variable path deeper than 25
segments now resolves to its default value.

A `$CURRENT_USER`, `$CURRENT_ROLE`, `$CURRENT_ROLES` or `$CURRENT_POLICIES` path in a query filter is
now held to `MAX_RELATIONAL_DEPTH`, the same as the fields it is fetched as, and is rejected with an
`InvalidQueryError` beyond it.

**Enforced `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` on incoming WebSocket messages ([#28521](https://github.com/directus/directus/pull/28521))**
A WebSocket message larger than `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` (default `1mb`) now closes the connection with
code `1009`. The setting applied only to REST bodies before this, leaving a message bounded by the
100MB `ws` allows on its own.

**Fixed websocket subscription delete events not enforcing read permissions ([#28522](https://github.com/directus/directus/pull/28522))**
WebSocket Subscription delete events now require read access to, at minimum, the `id` field and no item rules on the events collection. Users who don't meet these requirements will not receive delete events.

**Added proxy support via `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY` environment variables ([#28057](https://github.com/directus/directus/pull/28057))**
- Requests now go through the proxy set in `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`. If these variables are already set and S3 should be reached directly, add
